Are VPNs a scam, or do they still have a real purpose in 2026? In this video, David Bombal cuts through misleading VPN marketing and explains what a VPN actually hides, what it cannot protect, and whether you really need one. HTTPS encrypts the contents of most modern internet traffic, which means someone on the network generally cannot simply steal your passwords, banking details or private messages. However, HTTPS does not always hide which websites and services your devices are connecting to. David demonstrates how Server Name Indication, or SNI, can expose website destinations on a local Wi-Fi network and to an internet service provider, even when TLS 1.3 and encrypted DNS are being used.

title: Are VPNs a Scam? What They Hide and What They Don’t
